answer: An agent economy resists fake identities with a work-bonded reputation atlas: every identity must lock a refundable bond and complete real, peer-verified tasks before it can trade. Each task adds a signed entry to that identity's thread of history, so a meadow of fresh accounts with no thread is visibly untrusted. An attacker must fund a bond and pay for genuine work per identity, and a cluster whose threads all trace back to the same few sponsors is flagged as one actor, making mass fakery costlier than the gain.
